transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News in Cleveland, Ohio, I'm Dale Willman.
A federal judge Sunday dismissed a Justice Department lawsuit seeking to block the certification
of Alaska's U.S. Senate race if the incumbent Republican loses.
President Trump had ordered the DOJ to file the suit.
The race is among the country's most closely watched, and it could help determine which
party will control the chamber starting next January.
Millions of voters cast their ballots for the midterm elections during the early voting
this weekend, and more are expected to exercise those same rights as Tuesday's election day
gets closer, and PR's Hansi Luang has our reports.
>> Around the country, voters have returned more than 24 million mail-in ballots as of
Sunday.
They've also cast more than 30 million ballots in person at early voting sites, according
to the University of Florida's election lab.
All together, that's about 20% higher than the total early voting numbers for the last
midterm elections in 2022.
This year's numbers are expected to taper off as some states end early in-person voting
before election day.
For mail-in voters who haven't returned their ballots yet, it is likely too late now for
the U.S. Postal Service to deliver ballots in time for them to be received by Tuesday's
election day.
To make sure their votes get counted, voters can return their mail-in ballots at their local
election office or at any available ballot drop box instead.
Hansi Luang, NPR News.
>> Just two days before those midterm elections, Democratic Representative Haley Stevens revoked
her support Sunday for Democratic Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El Sayed.
Instead, she threw her support to El Sayed's Republican challenger, asked Sunday night
about the switch.
El Sayed says he's more interested in the rest of the state's residents.
>> At the end of the day, I actually don't think about Haley Stevens.
Like I said, the 9,999,998 people who are not those two, because you know what, I'm
just less interested in the politics of it all than I am in the policy of it all.
>> A number of Stevens' staff resigned after her announcements.
Over the weekend, intense rainfall across the American Southwest caused creeks and rivers
to swell dramatically in size, as Chris Clements, a member station KNAU reports, that's led
to a new round of flooding in the region.
>> Oak Creek near Sedona typically flows at a trickle this time of year.
This weekend, it was a churning, torrential brown river.
After it jumped its banks, it trapped residents in Sedona, leading to rooftop evacuations and
damaged property.
Jenny Kittridge manages a hotel along Oak Creek and says while her property hasn't been
damaged yet, as of Sunday afternoon, the creek was just below the deck of her lowest structure.
>> It was, yeah, the highest I have ever seen it in my 33 years here.
>> The downpour brought a fresh round of flooding to tribal communities like the Navajo and
Hopi reservations and caused the Verde and Salt Rivers to rise.
For NPR News, I'm Chris Clements, in Fox Ave.
>> And you're listening to NPR News.
The UN peacekeeping mission in western Sahara has ended after 35 years.
Funding for the mission ended after a Russian effort to extend the money for another year
was defeated, the end of the peacekeeping forces raising concerns about regional stability.
Morocco claims the mineral-rich caratroy, but the Polisario front wants independence.
Formula 1 racing has a new world champion, and as NPR's Adam Bierne reports, he's the
youngest ever.
>> With his race engineer congratulating him as he crossed the finish line at the Mexican
Grand Prix, all Kimi Antonelli could do was cry tears of joy.
>> That's what it sounded like on Apple TV.
Antonelli is only 20 years old.
That makes him the youngest F1 world champion by some distance.
He's dominated this season in his Mercedes.
Speaking right after getting out of the car, it was clear that this was the moment he's
been waiting for.
>> It's one that will live forever, and I just am speechless.
I'm trying to process what just happened.
>> Antonelli is also the first Italian champion since 1953.
Adam Bierne, NPR News.
>> The shakeups at the top of college football rankings continued this weekend, while Miami
remained in first place following its last-minute win over North Carolina.
Number 2 Ohio State dropped to 11th after losing to USC and was replaced at 2 by Georgia.
Utah climbed three places at number 3, followed by Notre Dame and UCLA.
Deanna dropped two slots to 6th with BYU in 7th, followed by Kentucky, Alabama, and Texas
in 10th.
Florida fell to number 25 after losing to Georgia.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: Federal judge dismisses Justice Department lawsuit seeking to block certification of Alaska Senate race
Millions of mail-in and in-person early votes cast ahead of Tuesday's midterm elections, with 20% increase over 2022
Democrat Haley Stevens withdraws support from Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, backs Republican challenger
Intense Southwest rainfall triggers flooding near Sedona, Arizona, and tribal communities including Navajo and Hopi reservations
UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara ends after 35 years following failed Russian funding extension
Kimi Antonelli, 20, becomes youngest Formula 1 world champion after winning Mexican Grand Prix
College football rankings shake up: Miami stays first, Ohio State drops to 11th after loss to USC
Florida falls to number 25 in college football rankings after losing to Georgia
